message.content:
The largest planet that has been observed so far is the protoplanet **HD 100546 b**.  
It orbits the young star HD 100546 and has a radius of roughly **2.5–3 times that of Jupiter** (about 30,000 km). Because it is still forming, its exact mass and radius are still being refined, but it remains the biggest planetary‑mass object that astronomers have detected in another solar system.
